findings.title: Down-side re-entry is keyed on the Up book's timestamp, throttling half the strategy
findings.claim: The same-book-snapshot dedup uses m.book_us (Up-token book clock) for BOTH sides, but Down fires are sourced from the Down token's own book whose clock is m.book_dn_us. After any fire in a market, new Down asks arriving as Down-book deltas (which update book_dn_us, not book_us) are rejected as 'same book snapshot' until an unrelated Up-book event happens; conversely an Up-book tick re-unlocks the SAME unchanged resting Down ask (bounded only by the claimed-vs-printed ledger).
findings.evidence: bot/strategy.py:240-243: `if self.last_book.get(m.slug) == m.book_us:\n    self.f["cooldown"] += 1\n    return None  # same book snapshot; would be a fictional second fill` — and the key is set identically for both sides at :280 and :293 (`self.last_book[m.slug] = m.book_us`). bot/state.py:685-691 shows Down events update only book_dn_us: `if m.asset_id_dn == asset_id: m.apply_delta(False, ...); m.book_dn_us = now_us()`.
findings.failure_scenario: z <= -2 in a 5m settle window; the losing Up token goes one-sided and static (the exact state described at strategy.py:209-214: 'the losing token loses its bid and quotes 0.001'). First Down fire records book_us=X. Fresh Down asks then stream in on the Down book (the code's own measurement: a qualifying market prints a median ~1,291 shares in-window and one entry captured only ~40, which is why re-entry exists, strategy.py:168-180) — every one is refused at line 240 because book_us is still X. The Down side is throttled to the Up book's event rate, exactly the 'timer cooldown suppressed 867 of 1,681 evaluations' failure (strategy.py:176-180) reintroduced for one whole side; in the older combined log Down was 150 of 340 fills, so this suppresses roughly half the signal surface in paper AND live. The reverse direction also holds: any Up-book delta unlocks a duplicate take of the unchanged Down ask (print-ledger-bounded fictional fills). Note run.py:761 has the same asymmetry — staleness gates check only (now - m.book_us), so a frozen Down book passes the 10s book-age check on the Up book's freshness.
findings.fix: Key the dedup on the book the candidate ask actually came from: for Down with dn_src=='book' compare/store m.book_dn_us (separate last_book entry per (slug, side)); for Up and for the mirror fallback keep m.book_us. Pass book_dn_us into the risk book-age check when trading off the real Down book.

findings.title: Strike latch races the oracle's ~1.6-2.8s delivery lag, freezing a wrong K forever
findings.claim: strike_avg latches k_fixed the first time it is called with now_us() >= t0, but Chainlink rounds arrive well after their round timestamps (measured on data/live/rtds: p50 1.62s, p90 2.09s, p99 2.47s, max 2.80s delivery lag, round stamps second-aligned). Any call landing in [t0, t0+~2.5s] latches K permanently missing the last 1-3 ticks of the [t0-w, t0) strike window, with the hold-integral silently extrapolating an older price over the gap.
findings.evidence: bot/state.py:638-639: `if now_us() >= m.t0_us:\n    m.k_fixed = ps / secs            # window closed: latch it`. Measured from data/live/rtds/2026-08-09_23 + 2026-08-10_00 jsonl (btc/usd, n=1102): payload round ts 1786320303000 (ms) received at t_local_us 1786320304144651, delivery lag p50 1.623s / p99 2.471s. The caller that hits this window is the 30s health loop (run.py:562 `await asyncio.sleep(5 if first else 30)`; run.py:568 `"K": (round(s.strike_avg(m), 2) ...)`), so ~2.5/30 ≈ 8% of markets latch inside the race window.
findings.failure_scenario: Health tick fires at t0+0.8s for a market whose strike-boundary second moved 3 sigma (exactly the regime this bot trades). The final ~2s of the strike window are held at the pre-move price, so K is off by (2/30)*delta. In z units the numerator error is tau*delta = 2s * 3*sigma_1s against a denominator sigma*sqrt(rem^3/3): ~0.9 z at rem=5s, ~2.0 z at rem=3s — enough to flip the z>=2 gate in either direction for the whole settle window. Because _settle_result also reuses the cached wrong m.k_fixed, the in-process paper grade shares the error and hides it; only Gamma scoring (score_paper.py) reveals the loss.
findings.fix: Latch only when now_us() >= m.t0_us + LATCH_GRACE_US with grace ~3.5s (> measured max delivery lag), or re-latch if a tick with round ts < t0 arrives after the first latch. Pre-latch reads already recompute correctly, so the grace costs nothing.

findings.title: _settle_result coverage guard is vacuous: settle grade back-extrapolates over feed gaps
findings.claim: settle_sum_so_far discards the `covered` and n_ticks quality flags that _integral returns, and run.py's only guard (`r_secs < m.w * 0.9`) can never trip unless the window has ZERO ticks, because _integral always returns secs = (b-a)/1e6 when any tick exists — so a settle window with one late tick and a multi-second oracle outage is graded as fully known, with the first tick's price back-extrapolated over the uncovered head and held prices over the gap.
findings.evidence: bot/state.py:646-647: `ps, secs, _, _ = self._integral(m.t1_us - w_us, min(t_us, m.t1_us))\nreturn ps, secs` — flags dropped. bot/state.py:596: `return total / 1e6, (b_us - a_us) / 1e6, len(pts), covered` — secs is the full span regardless of coverage; only the no-tick case (state.py:586-587) returns 0. run.py:235: `if K is None or r_secs < m.w * 0.9: return None`. Contrast strike_avg, which correctly requires `secs <= 0 or not covered or nticks < 3` (state.py:636).
findings.failure_scenario: Position taken at rem=25s; the RTDS socket dies at t1-20s and reconnects at t1-4s. The real oracle kept printing (and the venue settles on those prints), but the bot's ring buffer holds a t1-20s price across 16 of the 30 settle seconds. _settle_result computes r_secs=30, passes the 0.9w guard, and grades the fill on a fabricated average — feeding risk.on_settle_pnl and the daily-loss kill switch with a possibly sign-flipped P&L (per findings 9.6 the same machinery already mismatches the venue ~0.7% on btc even with good coverage). The headline +4.55c is Gamma-scored by src/score_paper.py so it is not contaminated, but the in-process kill switch and day_pnl seeding are.
findings.fix: Return and check the quality flags: in _settle_result require covered, nticks >= ~0.5*w*observed tick rate, and max intra-window gap below a few seconds; otherwise defer to the Gamma fallback that settle_loop already has.

findings.title: Calibration table bakes a 3-day up-drift: 8-12pt Up/Down asymmetry under a symmetric gate
findings.claim: The empirical z->P(Up) table is strongly asymmetric — at |z|=2.5 the favoured side wins 0.8878 when it is Up but only 0.8083 when it is Down (1-0.1917), and the skew is 8-12 points at every |z| — yet the bot gates both sides with the same zmin=2.0 and the same max_price=0.99. Measured on only 2026-08-07..09, the asymmetry is most plausibly sample drift (an up-trending window), so fair() hardcodes a 3-day regime into every ev_est and into the require_edge path; no per-side EV split of the +3.04c validation is published anywhere even though endgame_rollavg.py labels sides.
findings.evidence: bot/calib.py:20-31: POINTS = [(-3.5, 0.1833), (-2.5, 0.1917), (-1.5, 0.2860), ... (2.5, 0.8878), (3.5, 0.9159)] — P(Down|z<=-3.5)=0.8167 vs P(Up|z>=3.5)=0.9159; at ±1.5, 0.8382 vs 0.7140. bot/state.py:747-749 makes this the fair value: `z = self.zscore(m, t_us); emp = _p_up(z); return gauss if emp is None else float(emp)`. src/endgame_rollavg.py:132-146 carries a side column but no per-side EV appears in reports/findings.md.
findings.failure_scenario: By the bot's own table, a Down fill at ask 0.90 with z=-2.5 has EV = 0.8083 - 0.90 - 0.0063 fee = -9.8c/share, while the identical Up-side trade reads -1.9c — yet both pass the identical gate up to 0.99. If the pooled +3.04c is carried mostly by the Up leg, the live book runs a hidden losing Down leg at high asks; if instead the asymmetry is drift, then in a down-trending week the Up rows (measured in an up-drift) overstate Up win probability by ~8-10pts and every logged ev_est (and require_edge, if ever enabled) is wrong in the dangerous direction. Either branch is checkable in an hour from the existing prints data and neither has been checked.
findings.fix: Publish the per-side (Up vs Down) c/share and hit-rate split of the |z|>=2 validation before live; if the asymmetry is real, gate Down with a lower max_price or higher zmin; if it is drift, recalibrate the table on a longer, drift-balanced sample (or fit symmetric |z| buckets).

findings.title: require_edge threshold ignores the taker fee it is supposed to clear
findings.claim: The optional edge gate compares fv - ask against edge_min=0.02 with no fee term, although the venue fee 0.07*p*(1-p) is ~1.75c at mid prices — so the gate's real net-EV floor is ~0.3c, not the 2c the config name implies; the fee-aware ev_of() sits two lines above it and is used only for logging.
findings.evidence: bot/strategy.py:255-256 defines `def ev_of(fair, ask): return fair - ask - 0.07 * ask * (1 - ask)` but the gate at :276 is `if self.require_edge and fv - ba < self.edge_min: return None` (and :289 for Down) — no fee. Config note (bot/config.json rollavg_edge) says require_edge fires at avg px 0.389, where the fee is 0.0166, i.e. 83% of edge_min.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone flips require_edge=true to run the measured-clean variant (the config note explicitly keeps it as a paper-measurement flag): trades with fv - ask in [0.020, 0.037) at mid prices pass the gate with net EV between -1.7c and 0 after fee, diluting the +10.15c/share the flag was measured to deliver and corrupting the comparison the flag exists to make.
findings.fix: Gate on ev_of(fv, ba) >= edge_min (and ev_of(1-fv, ask_dn) for Down), i.e. subtract the fee inside the threshold, matching how the +10.15c figure should be defined.

findings.title: Down pricing never takes the cheaper of the real Down ask and the Up-bid mirror
findings.claim: best_ask_dn (and depth()) return the real Down-book ask whenever one exists and consult the 1-best_bid_up mirror only when the Down book is empty — but Polymarket's CLOB crosses a Down buy against complementary Up bids via minting, so the executable Down price is min(real_dn_ask, 1-bb_up). When the real Down book quotes wide (e.g. 0.995) while a thick Up bid implies 0.985, the max_price=0.99 gate rejects a trade that is actually executable, and fills are priced off the worse source.
findings.evidence: bot/state.py:267-274: `if self.asks_dn:\n    return self.asks_dn[0] + ("book",)\nbb, bbs = self.best_bid() ... return (round(1.0 - bb, 4), bbs, "mirror")` — unconditional preference; depth() at :286-294 has the same either/or structure and never merges the two ladders.
findings.failure_scenario: Config's own numbers: the 0.985-0.990 band holds 1.22M of 2.6M qualifying shares at +0.57c/share. Every settle-window snapshot where the real Down ask sits at 0.995+ while the Up bid implies <=0.99 is a rejected-but-executable trade in exactly that band; merging the two sources (min for the gate, interleaved ladders for depth) recovers that volume at no model change and strictly improves every accepted Down price.
findings.fix: In best_ask_dn return the minimum of the real Down ask and round(1-bb,4) (with its size), and have depth('Down', limit) merge both ladders sorted by price; keep dn_src for attribution.

result.clean_areas: Derived the contract math independently and verified the implementation term by term — the core is correct: (1) z algebra: phase-3 A|F_t ~ N((R+P_t*rem)/w, sigma^2*rem^3/(3w^2)) gives z=(R+spot*rem-K*w)/(sigma*sqrt(rem^3/3)), exactly state.py:775-777 and rollavg_pricer.py:92-96; phase-2 variance s+w/3 re-derived via the double integral of min(u,v) and matches state.py:772-773; the two branches are continuous at rem=w. Units are consistent throughout (numerator price-seconds, sd $*s). (2) Window boundaries: strike uses _integral(t0_us-w_us, t0_us) and settle uses _integral(t1_us-w_us, min(t,t1_us)), both half-open [a,b) with a tick at exactly a treated as in-force and a tick at b excluded — matches [t1-w,t1)/[t0-w,t0); tie-break `>= K` gives ties to Up per contract (run.py:237). (3) Timestamp units verified end-to-end against recorded data: RTDS payload timestamps are ms, second-aligned, strictly monotone with no duplicates in the sample (n=1102); run.py passes ms to on_oracle which stores us; backfill's *1000 matches; Binance T handled in ms with a us guard; vol.update gets ts_ms//1000 seconds correctly. (4) The S-vs-K gap asymmetry the brief warned about does not exist: BOTH averages come from the same time-weighted hold integral (_integral), so missing oracle seconds are handled symmetrically, and the count-vs-elapsed-seconds confusion (sum-of-ticks scaling) is fixed by integrating; observed-portion R plus spot*rem covers exactly w seconds against K*w. (5) sigma: sigma_rel is the oracle's own 1s log-return sd using only adjacent-second pairs (correctly avoiding sqrt(gap) inflation), multiplied by spot at the single right place (state.py:740, 769); the Binance fallback guard is complete — cold start with no oracle reference refuses to price, and the 3x band vs the last good oracle reading blocks the documented 5x under-read; memoization is per-second and harmless. (6) 15m family: m.w=60 is set from market duration, the gate min(window_s=60, m.w) yields 30s/60s correctly, and no 30 is hardcoded in the trading path. (7) min_rem_s floor and window-entry transition behave continuously; settle grading at t1+10s is complete given the measured max 2.8s delivery lag. (8) Fee formula 0.07*p*(1-p) matches venue facts in ev_of; Up/Down gates test the correct side's own ask (real Down book preferred, mirror as fallback with correct 1-bb arithmetic and correct mirrored print accounting). (9) Verified the headline +4.55c is scored against the venue's Gamma outcomes by src/score_paper.py, not by the bot's self-grading, so the paper result is not circular. (10) Checked the discrete-hold (jump-process) vs continuous-BM variance question at small rem: the continuous rem^3/3 overstates variance ~8-60% for rem<=5s, but the empirical p_up calibration and the z>=2 gate were both measured with the same formula, so the pipeline is self-consistent and the bias is conservative (misses late signals rather than manufacturing them) — not reported as a defect.

findings.title: Tape caps count opposite-direction and wrong-token prints: ~2x fill-size inflation
findings.claim: printed() — the sole evidence base for cap_tape and cap_life — filters prints only by price, never by aggressor side or economic direction. The tape merges both tokens (run.py:471 'if mirror: px = 1.0 - px') and run.py:468-474 discards the ev['side'] field the feed provides (verified present: all 570 recorded last_trade_price events carry side, 508 BUY / 62 SELL). With config max_price=0.99 the price filter passes essentially every print in the market (<=0.99 for Up buys, >=0.01 mirrored for Down buys), so prints of people SELLING into bids and of takers buying the OPPOSITE token are counted as volume our taker BUY could have won. Measured on the local capture (570 prints, 7 markets): counted/direction-correct volume = 2.0x aggregate, median 2.0x per market-token, p75 6.0x, max 21x, where direction-correct = BUY prints on the bought token + SELL prints on the complement (mint-cross supply). audit.md:24-25 shows the both-token merge was deliberately MATCHED to the tape backtest — meaning the $/day capacity projections inherit the same inflation; consistency with the backtest is not consistency with live FAK fills, which can only win same-direction flow.
findings.evidence: state.py:326-331: 'for t_us, px, sz in reversed(self.tape): ... if side == "Up": if px <= limit + 1e-9: tot += sz / elif px >= (1.0 - limit) - 1e-9: tot += sz' — no side test. run.py:468-474: 'elif et == "last_trade_price": px = float(ev["price"]); sz = float(ev.get("size", 0)); if mirror: px = 1.0 - px; self.state.on_trade(up_aid, px, ...)' — ev["side"] never read. Recorded event: '"price":"0.74","size":"1.35135",...,"side":"BUY"'.
findings.failure_scenario: Last 30s, z >= 2 says buy Up at ask 0.98 while the crowd is dumping: 100 shares of down-token BUY prints (people aggressively buying Down at 0.97-0.99, mirrored to up prices 0.01-0.03) plus up-token SELL prints land on the tape in 5s. cap_tape = 0.25*100 = 25 shares certified for our Up buy from purely opposite-direction flow; live, a FAK at 0.98 has zero of that flow available as counterpart. At the measured 2x aggregate inflation, everywhere the tape cap binds (per findings.md the 0.985-0.99 band holds 1.22M of 2.6M qualifying shares and is exactly where displayed depth is large so cap_tape governs), paper books ~2x the winnable size — the ~$2.4k booked and the $1.6-2.3k/day projection scale directly with that size. Caveat stated honestly: the capture covers rem 68-155s, not the settle window; in-window direction mix may differ, but any opposite-direction share is pure inflation.
findings.fix: Use the side field already in the feed: store (t_us, px, sz, taker_side, token) in m.tape; for a BUY of token X at limit L, count only BUY prints on X at px <= L plus SELL prints on the complement at complement-px >= 1-L. One-line change in _on_clob to pass ev['side'] through, and a two-branch filter in printed().

findings.title: cap_life ledger too dilute to stop double-dipping; effective participation ~5x intent
findings.claim: The 9fbc1bc fix for the known refresh-restore double-dip (consume() empties a level, the venue's next absolute-size delta or snapshot restores it) is cap_life = vol_participation * printed(side, limit, 0) - claimed, described in the code and commit as 'the binding realism cap'. It does not bind. printed(...,0) spans the market's WHOLE life (tape holds 400 prints; a 15m market has ~14 pre-window minutes of trading) and both directions (finding 1), while claiming only happens in the last 30-60s. Meanwhile cap_tape's rolling 5s window is re-armed by ANY book_us delta (strategy.py:248 gate; deltas arrive many times per second in the endgame — 49,962 price_change events in the ~85s recorded burst), so the SAME print justifies a fresh claim on every re-fire until it ages out: one print can be claimed ~5 times at vol_participation each, i.e. up to ~1.25x its size instead of 0.25x. The ledger only halts claims at 25% of whole-life two-direction volume, so in practice the per-market RISK caps (300 sh / $150) are what stop the paper broker, not any measure of winnable flow.
findings.evidence: run.py:693-695: 'cap_life = (f["vol_participation"] * m.printed(o["side"], o["limit"], 0) - m.claimed[o["side"]])'; run.py:684-686: 'cap_tape = f["vol_participation"] * m.printed(o["side"], o["limit"], now - int(f["vol_window_s"] * 1e6))'; state.py:219: 'self.tape = deque(maxlen=400)'; config.json: '"max_price": 0.99' makes the printed() price filter pass ~everything; strategy.py:248: re-fire allowed whenever book_us changed.
findings.failure_scenario: 15m market: 2,000 shares print pre-window, 500 in the settle window (~250 direction-correct). Intended cap: 0.25*250 = 62 shares. cap_life allows 0.25*2500 = 625; the $150 dollar cap binds first at ~153 shares @0.98 — a 61% effective participation in direction-correct flow, 2.5x the intended 25%. Concretely per print: a single 40-share print at 0.98 -> first fire claims 10; the level is restored by the next delta, book_us ticks re-arm the strategy, and 4 more fires inside the 5s window claim 10 each -> 50 shares booked off one 40-share print. The commit for the retroactive scorer (09c1469) concedes this decides 'whether the ~$2.4k/day run-rate projection was volume-inflated' — the forward-looking fix still leaves the same inflation live-vs-paper.
findings.fix: Make the ledger windowed and direction-aware: maintain per-side cumulative direction-correct printed volume since the market entered its settle window (or since first fire), and require claimed <= vol_participation * that quantity. That makes cumulative claims track contemporaneous winnable flow instead of lifetime both-direction volume, and subsumes the overlapping-window multi-count.

findings.title: Down-side re-fire gate keyed to Up-token book clock: same resting Down ask re-taken
findings.claim: The guard whose stated purpose is preventing 'a fictional second fill' on the same book state compares against m.book_us, which only up-token events update; Down-book quotes update m.book_dn_us (state.py:690). Both fire branches store m.book_us (strategy.py:294 and :306). In the settle window the up book ticks many times per second, so for Down signals taken from a real down book (dn_src=='book') the gate never suppresses: the identical resting down ask — whose consume() decrement is undone by every down-book refresh — is re-taken on every up-book delta, bounded only by the diluted caps of findings 1-2 and the risk caps. The gate is also wrong in the conservative direction: a genuinely new down ask arriving while the up book is quiet is suppressed as 'same book'.
findings.evidence: strategy.py:248: 'if self.last_book.get(m.slug) == m.book_us:' ... '# same book snapshot; would be a fictional second fill'; strategy.py:306 (Down branch): 'self.last_book[m.slug] = m.book_us'; state.py:686-690: up-token delta -> 'm.book_us = now_us()', down-token delta -> 'm.book_dn_us = now_us()'.
findings.failure_scenario: Down winning, z = -2.5, one MM rests 40 shares at 0.97 on the down book and never requotes. Up-token deltas tick ~5/s; each tick re-arms the gate, a new order queues, fires 410ms later against the refresh-restored 0.97 level, and consume() is undone by the next down-book snapshot. Subject to the tape caps passing (they do whenever any prints occur — finding 1 counts loser-side up prints toward Down buys), paper accumulates to the $150/market cap (~150 shares) off a single 40-share resting ask in a few seconds; live, one FAK takes at most the 40 (minus races) and subsequent FAKs find the level empty.
findings.fix: Track the gate per side and per book actually quoted: store (book_us if side=='Up' or dn_src=='mirror' else book_dn_us), or better, gate on the identity (price, size) of the specific ask targeted so an unchanged resting quote can never be ordered against twice.

findings.title: Delayed orders execute against arbitrarily stale books — no freshness check in _execute
findings.claim: _execute fills from m.depth() with no check of m.book_us / m.book_dn_us age. Book freshness is only enforced at SIGNAL time (risk.py:59 stale_book_s = 10.0 via inputs_ok), and the local book goes deliberately blind for the resubscribe gap every 240s cycle (run.py:403 't_end = time.time() + 240') and desyncs on queue-full drops (n_clob_drop) until the next full snapshot — snapshots are only ~2% of messages. A queued order firing during such a gap (via the 1s decide_loop) books a fill against a book that no longer exists; in the last 30s of a decided market, a several-seconds-old ask at <= 0.99 on the z-favoured side is usually already gone, so live FAKs would miss where paper fills.
findings.evidence: run.py:671: 'legs_avail = m.depth(o["side"], o["limit"])' — preceded only by the market-exists check and the flat reject draw; no recheck of book age anywhere in _execute. run.py:403: 't_end = time.time() + 240' (forced resub cycle); risk.py:59: 'self.stale_book_s = cfg.get("stale_book_s", 10.0)'.
findings.failure_scenario: Signal fires legitimately at book_age 0.2s, order queued; the clob ws hits its 240s cycle boundary and tears down; no deltas for ~1.5s; decide_loop's _process_pending executes the order at fire_us+~600ms against the pre-gap book showing 30 shares at 0.97 that were actually pulled during the gap. Roughly (gap ~1.5s / 240s) x (fraction of fires near a cycle boundary) of fills — order of 0.5-1% — are booked against vanished books, concentrated in fast markets where the miss would have been most likely. Low frequency, hence minor; the same one-line check also covers the n_clob_drop desync case, which is unbounded in duration.
findings.fix: In _execute, treat a stale view as the venue's re-validation reject: if now - (m.book_us if side Up/mirror else m.book_dn_us) > ~1.5s, count as ask_gone miss instead of filling.

result.clean_areas: TIMING (checked hard, correct): fills are never taken at decision time — taker signals queue with fire_us = now + (venue_hold_ms 250 + rtt_ms)*1000 and _execute runs against the book as of fire time or later (run.py:618-654), so realized cancels/decay/competing consumption up to T+~410ms are captured by construction; using the FULL rtt (not one-way) and executing at the first event/1s-tick at-or-after fire_us both bias conservative. The limit is the ask seen at decision, so price improvement is possible but marketability is re-tested against the delayed book (ask_gone miss otherwise) — faithful FAK+hold semantics. participation=0.5 is applied ON TOP of the delayed book as a race-share haircut, not as a substitute for survival, so the measured 63-69%/50% survival is not double-granted. reject_rate is drawn before sizing (run.py:666) — for a flat hazard the ordering is immaterial. UNITS/WALK: o['size'] is shares end-to-end (q_usd = size*limit confirms); the fill walks legs cheapest-first taking at most participation per level, books each leg at its own level price, logs true vwap, and broker cost = sum sh*(px + 0.07*px*(1-px)) matching the venue fee (paper.py:65-73) — no touch-price flattery, no unit mixups. MIN SIZE: want < 5 rejects the whole order after caps (run.py:698); the walk guarantees got == want, so no sub-5 partial can ever book; live's placement-time orderMinSize applies to the >=5-share order we would send, so paper is conservative here. SELF-COUNTING: paper fills are never appended to m.tape or fed back through on_trade_print — the tape is fed exclusively by venue last_trade_price events (run.py:468-474, state.py:694-701); no self-counting exists. DUAL-TOKEN DOUBLE PRINTS: tested on the recorded capture — 570 trades carry 570 distinct transaction_hashes with zero same-tx prints on both tokens of one market, so the mirror does NOT double-count a single match. CONSUME: within-burst double-spend is correctly prevented and depth()/consume() agree on which ladder (up asks, down asks, or mirrored up bids) is decremented, including the 4dp mirror rounding; a tape rolling off maxlen=400 can only shrink caps (conservative). EXPOSURE ACCOUNTING: in-flight orders count toward sizing and the opposite-side guard, and a kill/cool-off flushes the pending queue — no free fills after a stop. ADVERSE SELECTION (survival conditional on the signal being wrong): there is no accounting beyond flat participation, but this is explicitly disclosed as unmodelled in findings.md 8.6 and partly mitigated by construction since the sim fills off the real delayed book (realized conditional cancels are in the data); I attempted an empirical conditional test on data/live/books but the loser-side sample in the 0.92-0.99 band is n=6 snapshots — too thin to quantify locally (winner-side: 72% reachable / 90% size surviving at +400ms in 0.92-0.99, n=456; 51%/40% in 0.80-0.92, n=362).
